# `prepayment: 20` beside a `Transaction` block naming two splits that leave
# nothing over.
#
# A grouped block may carry `prepayment:` — a residue is the payment's rather
# than any one split's, and on a printed page that line is the only place a
# residue can be stated at all. What it is weighed against is the receivable
# splits of the transaction the block does **not** name.
#
# Here it names both, and they come to exactly what the invoice owes, so there
# is nothing left over and no split for the declared 20.00 to be. It is the
# figure being wrong that is refused, not the key being present.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal saying the declared figure does not
# match the residual splits, which sum to nothing.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    memo: "Wire"
    prepayment: 20
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
      PaymentSplit "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
